title: Return of the Ape Man

evidence.note: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, Jan-Dec 1972 (Vol 26, Parts 12-13) lists: THE RETURN OF THE APE MAN, a photoplay in 6 reels by Monogram Pictures Corp., © 13May44, L12655. Renewed by Allied Artists Pictures Corp. (PWH, proprietor of copyright in a work made for hire), 5May72, R528467. This matches the 1944 Monogram film, so the 1944 copyright was renewed in its 28th year.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Vol 26, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, 1972 (archive.org)

evidence.note: This is a sound film. The recorded track was part of the film as registered and renewed, so it follows the print's status. I did not research any separate music publication rights.

editorial:
The Return of the Ape Man was registered by Monogram Pictures Corp. on 13 May 1944 as a six-reel photoplay. Allied Artists Pictures Corp., the company that carried on Monogram's rights, renewed the copyright on 5 May 1972 as proprietor of a work made for hire (renewal R528467). The catalog volume for that year lists the renewal, so the film is not in the public domain under the renewal-absence route that frees many 1944 B-pictures.

The film circulates widely online in transfers of unclear provenance, and a copy being easy to find does not mean it is cleared. A renewed 1944 film is protected for 95 years from publication, so US protection runs through the end of 2039. A creator who wants to use clips or the full film needs a licence from whoever now holds the Monogram/Allied Artists library rights, or should wait for the term to expire.
faq: Is The Return of the Ape Man (1944) in the public domain in the US?

No. The Catalog of Copyright Entries for 1972 lists a renewal by Allied Artists Pictures Corp., filed 5 May 1972 under R528467, for the 1944 Monogram film. That renewal extended the copyright, so the film is still protected.
Why do copies of it appear on the Internet Archive and YouTube?

Uploaders often assume that a low-budget 1944 film lapsed into the public domain. This film did not, because its renewal was filed. Being hosted online does not clear the rights, and I did not verify any of the online copies as licensed.
